transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Amy Held.
The Trump administration is blaming Congress for not providing funding for outdated technology
behind Friday's nationwide ground stop, demanding $50 billion for an upgrade.
Democrats are demanding more answers.
They say FAA and DOT staff will deliver a briefing about the money Congress has already
approved for safety upgrades that has not been spent.
Meantime, the misery goes on at the nation's airports.
More than 6,000 flights disrupted so far today.
Steve Futterman reports.
At Los Angeles International, Marilyn Mathis and her husband spent much of the day trying
to get home to Houston.
Like many others, she tried to come up with ways to sleep at the airport.
I'm sleeping on the floor, sitting on your suitcases, head up against the wall.
How was that?
Not good.
Not good.
Federal officials say they hope to have things back to normal by Sunday night, but there
could be residual effects for a few additional days.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman in Los Angeles.
Israel says it's killed a top Hamas commander in southern Gaza.
Hamas confirmed the Israeli airstrike overnight, calling it a "cowardly assassination."
NPR's Lauren Freire reports from Tel Aviv.
The Israeli military released grainy black and white aerial footage of a man walking
alone on a street lined with what looked like tents, then an explosion and debris.
It identified the target as Sameer Mahmoud Hassan Abu Yunis.
Hamas confirms he was one of its senior commanders, a member of the organization's military wing
since 1991.
Hamas says he helped plan and supervise the October 7th attacks, and pledged that his
quote "blood shall not be in vain."
Since those 2023 attacks and the Israeli assault on Gaza that followed, health officials say
Israeli attacks have killed more than 74,000 people in Gaza.
Lauren Freire, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
Investors are keeping an eye on Nvidia this week, this time looking past its former CEO's
scandals and toward the chipmaker's earnings.
NPR's Stephen Bizaha reports that investors are also gearing up for the artificial intelligence
company Anthropic's initial public offering.
There has been a pattern over the past few years on the AI side of the stock market.
Investors get worried the industry is overvalued.
Then Nvidia shares another quarter of jaw-dropping earnings beating Wall Street expectations.
Tuesday Nvidia will again report its latest earnings during an especially tough time for
the industry and the company.
The tech-heavy NASDAQ is down about 7.5% over the month.
Nvidia stock value has also fallen sharply after the ouster of its scandal-plagued CEO
Jensen Wong last week.
Anthropic is looking to join that shaky stock market with an initial public offering planned
for later this week.
The price Anthropic's currently signaling would value the company at $1.4 trillion.
Stephen Bizaha, NPR News.
This is NPR News.
A meteorite that came crashing through the roof of a house in Texas earlier this year
is now on display at a museum in Houston.
Michael Adkisson from Houston Public Media reports the space rock is in a new exhibit
called "Fall to Earth."
A streak of light and a sonic boom sounded over Houston earlier this year.
A meteor, weighing a ton, broke apart and exploded, sending meteorites to the ground,
including one about the size of a fist that crashed into Sherry James' home.
I'd say that's the meteorite on that floor.
It's just my mind just going everywhere.
I went back in and I went and did the crazy thing, I kicked it.
And I'm like, yeah, that's a rock, because I was scared to touch it, so I wasn't touching
it.
Researchers now estimate that meteorite is 4.5 billion years old, likely originally coming
from the asteroid belt.
It's now on display at the Houston Museum of Natural Science.
For NPR News, I'm Michael Adkisson in Houston.
The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inducted a new class comprising 18 musicians.
Among those paid tribute, Phil Collins.
Collins is part of an esteemed group to have been inducted more than once his first time
with his old band, Genesis, in 2010.
Last night, he was given a standing ovation.
Such an outpouring of emotion.
I had tears in my eyes, I'm going to be honest.
Also inducted Oasis, Queen Latifah, and Iron Maiden.
Students only become eligible 25 years after their first release.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Trump administration blames Congress for outdated FAA technology behind nationwide ground stop, seeks $50 billion
Thousands of flights disrupted at U.S. airports, with stranded travelers like Marilyn Mathis in Los Angeles
Israel says it killed senior Hamas commander Sameer Mahmoud Hassan Abu Yunis in southern Gaza airstrike
Nvidia faces investor scrutiny ahead of earnings amid CEO Jensen Huang's ouster and Anthropic's upcoming IPO
Meteorite that crashed through Sherry James' Texas roof is on display at Houston Museum of Natural Science
Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inducts 18 musicians, including Phil Collins, Oasis, Queen Latifah, and Iron Maiden
